rule.text: Mandate: Ensure the efficient, secure, and controlled delivery of IT services by managing the full lifecycle of Incidents, Service Requests, Changes, Problems, and Configuration Items (CIs) in strict accordance with defined policies and best practices.
First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.
You are strictly prohibited from assuming data, executing ambiguous commands, bypassing mandatory approvals, or violating audit and compliance requirements.
Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.
User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.
Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.
You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.
When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.
Complete each task in a logical, and efficient execution flow.

The assignment should generally follow broad team tendencies, where L1 Field Support → hardware-type issues, L1 Infra Team → software-related matters, L1 IT Support → Techinal supports like application setups, device configurations, mobile apps, application setup/configuration issues etc.. L1 Infra Team → infrastructural such as workstation or furniture setups, L1 Service Desk → Team covers general IT needs that don’t fit cleanly into hardware or software, and Service Desk Operations picks up cases where the requester isn’t sure what the issue is or whom to contact, though these boundaries may overlap depending on how the problem is described.
Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policy_questions.question: "First you must check the user information": which user is meant (the logged-in user, the caller, both), and what must happen when the role cannot be confirmed?
The Administrator row has no Critical Restrictions cell. Are there really no restrictions, including on approving a Change Request, which only the Manager row names?

The Manager grant names incident, problem, change, knowledge. Is the Manager forbidden on every other write tool: users, groups, locations, incident templates, CIs, services, SLA definitions, notifications, Incident SLA records?
The Agent grant does not name users, groups, locations, incident templates, SLA definitions, notifications or Incident SLA records. Is the Agent forbidden on the write tools of all of these?
Section 5 is titled "Configuration and Service Management (CMDB)". Does the Agent's CMDB grant include services and service offerings? The package assumes yes and does not forbid them.

Do the grants on incident, change and knowledge include the link tools (child incidents, knowledge links, change mappings, affected CIs)? The package assumes yes, although the Manager has only READ on CMDB and link_affected_ci_to_incident touches a CI.
The Reporter row says "view and update" but also "their own submitted". May a Reporter call create_incident? The package does not forbid it.
Which fields of their own incident may a Reporter update? The Agent row names assignment, state and resolution; the Reporter row names none.

May a Reporter read records other than their own incidents and Public Knowledge (users, groups, services, changes, problems, SLAs)? The row grants nothing else but forbids only other users' records, CMDB and internal work notes. The package forbids only CI read tools.
Which field decides that a record is the Reporter's own submitted record? create_incident has caller_id, the user affected, who may be another person, and no field for the user who submits.
Does "CMDB" in the Reporter restriction also cover list_incident_affected_cis and service or service offering reads? The deny rule covers only configuration item tools.
Which tools change "system administration settings", which the Agent cannot do?

"Requests", "Service Requests" and "Tasks" have no tool in the tool list. Does the policy mean incidents here, or do these parts have no effect? The same question holds for the service_catalog_item in 5.2:2.
The Manager "Can reassign incidents/requests" and the Agent "Can update assignment". Is reassigning an incident that already has an assignee open to both roles?
Priority "is determined automatically by the system", but create_incident stores the default planning when priority is omitted. Must the agent pass the matrix value, or leave priority out?
If a request states a priority that differs from the matrix, must the agent halt under Policy Violation, or create the record with the matrix value? May any role override it?
When impact or urgency changes on update_incident or update_problem, must priority be set again from the matrix? The rules check only the create tools.
SLAs are aligned based on priority, but applies_to_priority of an SLA definition does not accept planning. Does an incident of priority planning have no SLA?
"halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing": what does pausing mean for the agent, ending the task, or waiting for the next user message?
Which endpoints are the "approved batch endpoints"? Is add_child_incidents one of them?
"return the list": which list is meant when a request is ambiguous, the records that match?

A mandatory field that is an identifier (caller_id) is missing: 1:4 says state which field is required, 1:7 says perform lookups. Which holds when a name is given but no ID, and which when nothing is given?
"all mandatory fields": only section 3 names mandatory fields. Which are mandatory for the other records and for update calls: the tool's required list?
"The same is the case of optional or default arguments": may the agent pass an optional argument the request does not state, for example a tool default such as category?
A call gives assigned_to but no assignment_group. Is the group of the incident the "specified" one, or is the membership not checked?

3.3:9 says an incident stays resolved for a mandatory 72-hour customer confirmation period before it closes automatically, and a manual closure needs the Manager role "present". 3.3:22 says resolved → closed happens after a "time window 72 hours or someone decides". Who may close before 72 hours: only a Manager, or anyone who decides? What does "present" mean, and how does the customer confirm?
The tools accept status canceled for an incident; the policy lists five states without it. Is canceled forbidden? The transition rule has no edge to it.

Section 9 lists resolution_code values fixed, workaround, not_reproducible, closed_by_caller; the tools accept only Duplicate, Known Error, No resolution provided, Resolved By Caller, Resolved By Problem, Resolved By Change, Solution Provided, Workaround Provided, User error. Which list holds, and is there a mapping?

Change type (standard, normal, emergency) has no argument in create_change or update_change, only category and cab_required. Where is the type recorded? Must cab_required follow from it? The text now says normal requires planning/approval → CAB approval: is cab_required true for a normal change?

The description of create_problem writes values in capitals (NEW, HIGH), its argument descriptions in lower case; the policy uses lower case. Which case is correct? The rules use lower case and stay at remind.
What counts as a "recurring incident pattern" (how many incidents, in what time) and as a "major incident" (priority critical)?
There is no incident_to_problem related list in the tools. Is the link made by the problem argument of update_incident?
There is no workaround_notes field. Into which field of a linked incident (worknotes, description) and of a knowledge article is it published, and which articles are "relevant"?
May a Problem that is already past fix_in_progress get a corrected workaround without going back to fix_in_progress?
What proves that the permanent fix was "successfully implemented": a mapped change with status closed and close_code successful, or status implement or review?
Status in_stock is in neither sentence of the CI State rule. Is it forbidden, as "Only" says? The rule forbids it.
Which incident statuses are "active Incidents"? May an in_stock or retired CI be linked to a resolved or closed incident? The rule does not look at the incident.

"Metrics tracked are limited to response_time and resolution_time": the tools have metric with values response and resolution, and target_mins. Are response_time and resolution_time the metric values response and resolution? Does this forbid any argument of an SLA definition?

Who pauses the SLA timer, the system or the agent? If the agent, the Agent, Manager and Reporter grants name no SLA record, so the grant rules and the duty conflict for update_incident_sla_details. Nothing decides, so both stay at remind.
The SLA Pause text says the Incident is in "stage = on_hold", but incident has status, not stage. Is status meant? The rule assumes yes.

The escalation flag on the Incident (6:9) has no argument in update_incident. Is the flag set by recording worknotes = Escalated (6:12)? Who decides that "SLA breach risk exists" or "High business risk/impact"?
"an automatic notification sent to the Manager": does the system send it, or must the agent call send_notification? Which Manager (the manager_id of the group, any user with role manager)?
"Public Knowledge" and "published": does Public also mean visibility = external? May a Reporter find a published internal article?
How is a knowledge article "relevant" or "matching" (which search field, how close)?

When a Reporter creates an incident, 7:2 requires a knowledge link, but the Reporter grant does not name link_knowledge_to_incident, and the Reporter finds only published articles. Is the link still made, and by whom? Nothing decides, so both stay at remind.
"any user being ... updated is users.active = true": does this forbid update_user_details on an inactive user, including setting active back to true?

Which are the "mandatory dependencies" to verify before closing a record? The text gives one example (an Incident cannot close if its related change_request is not closed) and 4.3:6 names one for a Problem. Which other dependencies and records are meant, and which change states count as closed?

"All work logs (work_notes and activity_log)" must include sys_created_on and user_id, but worknotes is one text argument of the incident and problem tools, activity_log has no tool, and sys_created_on is not an argument. Must the agent write the timestamp and user_id into worknotes?

The Administrator row has no closing "|", so the converter reads the Manager row as the table header of the Agent and Reporter rows and gives it no statement of its own. The Manager grant rule (r_manager_grant) therefore has no statement id; its quote is copied from the policy file. Please add the closing "|" to the Administrator row, or confirm the Manager row is as written.

Mandatory Inputs gives defaults for channel (chat), impact (low) and urgency (low), but 1:9 says never assume optional or default arguments. The package takes the defaults of 3.1:3 as stated by the policy. Is that right?
